To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) nanostructuration of oxides and sulfides can enhance the thermoelectrical properties, (ii) layered oxides and sulfide can exhibit high thermoelectric figures of merit, (iii) the presence of ‘rattle’ atoms in the structure can enhance thermoelectric properties, (iv) the thermoelectric figure of merit is strongly dependent on the chemical composition, and (v) the thermoelectrics properties of a given material can be tuned by changing the chemical
the thermoelectric efficiency can be enhanced by nanostructuration and by using materials with complex crystal structures, such as layered materials and materials with a large number of atoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new thermoelectric oxysalts, sulfides and chalcogelides, the understanding of their thermoelectric properties and their optimization.
the discovery, the synthesis, the structural, the electronic and the thermoelectric characterization of new materials.
the discovery and understanding of new materials for energy conversion, with the aim of improving the efficiency of the thermoelectric conversion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the thermoelectric community has to continue its efforts on the search of new thermoelectric material families and on the understanding of the mechanisms leading to the enhancement of the thermoelectric figure of merit.

the thermoelectric performance of a material depends on the nature and the number of atoms in the lattice, the crystal structure, the electronic structure (band structure, presence of electronic correlations, etc…), the presence of ‘rattle’ atoms, the nano-structuration of the material, the doping, and the presence of interfaces.
there is no universal rule for the design of new thermoelectric oxysulfides and oxyselenides, and that each family of materials should be studied separately.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermoelectric performances of sulfides and oxides are comparable, and that the optimization of the Seebeck coefficient is the most efficient way to enhance the ZT values of these compounds.

thermoelectric materials with a high power factor are generally characterized by a large number of atoms in the unit cell (more than 20), a complex crystallographic structure (low dimensional structures) and the presence of a large number of ‘rattler’ atoms.
the most important factor for improving thermoelectric performance in these materials is the presence of a large number of atoms in the unit cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the search for new thermoelectrics is a challenging task, and that a large number of parameters must be taken into account, such as the crystallographic structure of the materials, the electronic structure, the presence of ‘rattle’ atoms, etc.
the thermoelectric efficiency of a material is strongly related to its structure, and that nanostructuration and low dimensionality are two important parameters to enhance the Seebeck coefficient.
the thermoelectric performance of these materials is strongly dependent on their chemical composition, their crystal structure and the presence of ‘rattle’ atoms.
